concept: Flex Tooling Migration Terraform K8s CLI

claims.text: The Flex resource documentation recommends mongodbatlas_advanced_cluster for managing Flex because it also supports tenant and Dedicated clusters. The migration guide likewise recommends advanced_cluster for converted shared-tier deployments, although its Serverless-to-Flex subsection contains conflicting resource recommendations. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Avoid leaving one converted Atlas cluster bound to multiple Terraform resource addresses: HashiCorp warns that duplicate imports can cause unwanted behavior, and the Atlas guide explicitly removes the former Serverless address when replacing it with the imported resource. (high confidence)

For mixed Terraform and Kubernetes tooling, Pulumi recommends assigning ownership by namespace, resource type, or workload boundary because overlapping tools can overwrite desired state. Applying that ownership discipline during a Flex tooling migration is a methodological inference; the article does not test MongoDB Flex or establish a Flex-specific reconciliation failure. (low confidence)

Flex imports use a provider-defined ID in PROJECT_ID-FLEX_CLUSTER_NAME form. Terraform's import command binds that existing object to the specified resource address; the ID format comes from the provider, rather than Terraform itself. (high confidence)

MongoDB documents January 22, 2026 as the end of general tooling support for M2/M5 and Serverless. Existing M2/M5 clusters migrated to Flex; Serverless deployments could become Free, Flex, or Dedicated, so automation must first identify the actual target type. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

For an already converted Serverless-to-Flex deployment, the provider guide describes importing the existing cluster, updating references, removing the obsolete serverless state binding, and confirming a plan with no changes. It warns that retaining the obsolete binding can plan deletion. HashiCorp separately requires each remote object to have only one Terraform resource address; treat import and old-binding cleanup as a controlled state reconciliation, with plan review before applying. (high confidence)

A March 24, 2025 community report encountered CANNOT_USE_FLEX_CLUSTER_IN_CLUSTER_API after converting an M0 deployment to Flex. The author mentioned updating a Terraform module to 1.29.0 and reported that importing the converted cluster resolved the state synchronization problem; the thread does not identify a Terraform provider version. This is a historical incident, not evidence that current advanced_cluster resources lack Flex support. (low confidence)

The Atlas migration page requires removing obsolete M2/M5 and Serverless CLI commands and configures Kubernetes Flex deployments through spec.flexSpec with operator 2.12.0 or later. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The Flex migration guidance tells CLI users to remove M2/M5 and Serverless commands, including obsolete Serverless continuous-backup steps. It directs workloads requiring private endpoints or continuous backup and point-in-time restore to Dedicated clusters. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Provider release 2.14.0, dated July 15, 2026, includes a fix for intermittent tenant/Flex-to-Dedicated upgrade failures; PR 4548 explains that Atlas could transiently return IDLE with the old TENANT/FLEX provider and replaces one retry with bounded polling until both IDLE and Dedicated are observed. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-15)

For converted clusters managed through Spacelift, its documented resource-import route runs terraform import as a task on the owning stack; this supplies a platform-specific way to perform the state reconciliation required by the Atlas migration guide. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

A Terraform state rollback does not reverse an Atlas tier conversion: Spacelift explicitly says rollback changes only state, while the Atlas guide separately describes reconciling state after the infrastructure has already converted. (medium confidence)
